projects.heroTitle: At 4Herfrika, we believe in doing, not just dreaming.
projects.heroDescription: Our programs are grassroots-driven, impact-focused, and designed to connect ambitious women across Africa with real mentorship, networks, and resources. Whether you are pursuing technology, business, medicine, law, agriculture, or any field that shapes Africa's future — we help you navigate your chosen path with confidence, purpose, and the leadership skills to succeed.
projects.introDescription: 4Herfrika is a community of ambitious women making local impacts for global change.
projects.introFullDescription:
4Herfrika is a community of ambitious women making local impacts for global change.
We believe the most powerful lever for change in Africa isn't a single skill — it's access to people who have walked the path ahead.
Whether you're a mentee seeking guidance, a mentor ready to invest in the next generation, or a partner believing in our vision — you're part of a movement that's reshaping what leadership looks like across African campuses.
At 4Herfrika, we give you the skill, the certification, the platform and a support system you need to climb global stages.

seo.title: Year 2 Impact Report: Two Steps Forward — 4HerFrika
seo.description: 4HerFrika's second year: registered with the CAC, three academies, menstrual health outreach from Makoko to Ogbomoso, and a mentorship programme open to every member.

impactYear2.heroDescription: Building women of global impact. This year we registered, opened three academies, took menstrual health outreach from Makoko to Ogbomoso, and opened mentorship to every member.
impactYear2.heroAlt: 4HerFrika participants in pink shirts standing together outdoors on campus

note.first: Last year we named what we needed.
note.p1: Last year we spoke about what we needed: a way to measure what we were doing beyond how it felt, a way to fund it beyond our own resources, and a playbook so a campus in Bamenda could run the same way as a campus in Lagos, without the team on every call.
note.p2: In October we registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission. 4HerFrika stopped being a beautiful idea living on a website and became something recognised by the law, accountable to more than our own conscience.
note.p3: In January we quietly piloted a mentorship programme, because we wanted to test the ground before we asked anyone to put their weight on it. The ground held, so we opened it to everyone.
note.p4: We also reached further than we built. Girls in Makoko held boxes of sanitary pads over their heads like trophies. A young woman in Lagos finally asked a doctor the question about her own body she had carried alone for years. A campus in Ogbomoso broke a silence around menstrual health older than any of us.
note.p5: We are not finished, and we were never trying to be this year. We were trying to take the next honest step, and then the one after it. Together, we're taking two steps forward.
note.name: Ademide Ademola

previously.label: Previously, in Year 1
previously.body: One campus in Nigeria became 25 across five countries, and over 3,000 girls were mentored. “This is just the beginning,” we said. We meant it.

registered.title: Registered with the CAC
registered.body: We became a registered organisation, so partners can sign real agreements with us instead of handshake promises.

academies.title: Three academies, one roof
academies.body: Tech, Business and Climate, giving volunteers somewhere to return to between outreach days.

partnerships.title: Partners who stood beside us
partnerships.body: TEDx Ajegunle gave us a stage, FUSE shaped the Tech Academy, Google Developer Group joined us at TechFiesta, and Hult Prize opened a door into entrepreneurship.

mentorship.title: Becoming Her, piloted
mentorship.body: A mentorship programme tested quietly for two seasons before we asked anyone to trust it publicly.

built.closing: None of it lives in a filing cabinet. What got built didn't stay built. It walked out the door.

outreach.quote: No girl or woman should miss an opportunity, or feel smaller than she is, because of her period.
outreach.quoteSource: The sentence the Menstrual Health Awareness Movement was built on.

makoko.title: Menstrual Health Awareness Movement
makoko.body: With Sanitary Aid NG, Civic Hive, Skygirls and The GirlsComm, more than 300 girls came, 300 pads were given out, and period myths were taken apart in front of girls who had never heard them challenged.

giveToGain.title: Give to Gain
giveToGain.body: Around International Women's Day we took the conversation into secondary schools and widened it to gender-based violence, named plainly and without shame.

rhythm.title: A rhythm, not a one-off
rhythm.body: Another pad distribution, another room of girls leaving with something they didn't walk in with, each one led by campus women who arrived before the buses and stayed after the last box was gone.

unilag.name: University of Lagos
unilag.highlight: 347 members, 47 of them new this year
unilag.body: In May, an Endometriosis webinar kept 25 participants for the full hour with a health professional. In July, with the Nigeria Association of Accounting Students and Final Ledger, Pad a Girl reached 100 students.

kwasu.name: Kwara State University
kwasu.highlight: Endometriosis and Pad a Girl programming
kwasu.body: The campus ran the same Endometriosis and Pad a Girl programming this year, in step with the wider movement.

lautech.name: LAUTECH
lautech.highlight: Half the members active, one of the strongest rates in the network
lautech.body: Rhythms of Connection put members in rooms with local creatives. In April, Women Techmakers Ogbomoso opened free tech learning. In May, a World Menstrual Hygiene Day campaign broke hostel-room myths, and a weekly quote series kept everyone talking all year.

campuses.closing: We stayed at 25+ campuses in five countries this year and put the work into growing each one. Every campus runs its own outreach, with its own partners, on its own calendar, and for the first time one thing was open to every member wherever she studies.

mentorship.body: We tested it quietly for two seasons, learning what a girl needs when she asks “who do I call now?” At the anniversary we opened it properly. Every member can now reach someone a few steps ahead of her on the road she's walking.

anniversary.title: Two years old, further along than that.
anniversary.body: Ese, Hus, Ademide and Faree led a fireside chat with women who have already built what our members are building. CVs got real feedback, LinkedIn profiles got sharper, and Becoming Her had its first public teaser.
anniversary.partners: Civic Hive, Ordina, FUSE, Moniepoint and Cowrywise, with the 4HerFrika UNILAG and LASUCOM chapters.
anniversary.stride: The celebration continues on 27 November 2026 at The Stride Conference, Civic Hive, Lagos: our first leadership conference, themed “Stride: Women Leading Africa Forward”.

numbers.pendingNote: These are the figures verified so far. The full count across every campus is on its way, and this page will be updated when it lands.

lessons.title: What we learned
lessons.intro: None of those numbers came easy, and pretending otherwise would make the next ones less believable.

hard.title: What was hard
hard.body: Exams pulled members away, sponsorships took longer to close than we expected, and some campuses had members spread across too many communities.

worked.title: What worked
worked.body: Partnering with student organisations already on campus, staying in touch with members even when few replied, and handing more of the work to campus leads.

next.title: What we're carrying forward
next.body: Starting sponsorship talks before the need is urgent, building a real fundraising plan, and keeping the standard reporting we began this year.

give.intro: Vague asks are easy to ignore, so here is exactly where your support goes.

donations.title: Open donations
donations.body: Outreach logistics, transport and the anniversary event: venue, refreshments, plaques for speakers who give their evening for free, and banners.

pads.title: Pad Support Movement
pads.body: Sanitary pads for the next Makoko, the next campus, the next girl who shouldn't miss school over something this solvable.

inKind.title: In-kind support
inKind.body: Clothing, shoes, bags and personal care items, the small things that let a girl walk into a room without carrying shame in with her.
inKind.cost: Get in touch to give items

goal.body: Twenty-five campuses, five countries and over 3,000 girls mentored since the first one. The distance to two million by 2030 is real, and we won't pretend otherwise. This year we registered, built three academies, opened mentorship and reached girls in rooms that had never had this conversation.

next.funding: Funding that doesn't depend on any single source.
next.playbook: A playbook thorough enough that a new campus can open without waiting for the centre.

thanks.leads: To Adeyemi Aliyat Omowunmi, Elizabeth Agbana and Oluwatosin E. Idowu, who led their campuses through a year that asked more of them than any spreadsheet can show.
thanks.partners: To TEDx Ajegunle, FUSE, Google Developer Group, Hult Prize, Sanitary Aid Initiative, Civic Hive, Skygirls, The GirlsComm, Women Techmakers Ogbomoso, Rhythms of Connection, Final Ledger and everyone who showed up when it mattered.
thanks.girls: And to every girl who walked into a room this year and asked the question she had been carrying alone.
thanks.closing: The next step is already testing the ground. Come put your weight down with us.
